mekki-muskil:1-1.t: The saying of the Exalted {ذَات بَيْنكُم}: the original form of ذات according to the Basrans is ذوات; the wāw was changed into an alif and then dropped because it was quiescent and the alif after it was quiescent, so ذات remained. This is shown by the saying of the Exalted in the dual: ذواتا أفنان, where the wāw returned to its original form. All the scholars and the Qurʾān readers pause on ذات with tāʾ, except Abū Ḥātim, who allowed pausing on it with hāʾ. Quṭrub said: the pause on ذات is with hāʾ wherever it occurs, because it is the hāʾ of the feminine of ذي مال ("possessor of wealth").

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying {وجلت قُلُوبهم}: the imperfect of وجل is يوجل. Among the Arabs there are those who say ييجل, replacing the wāw with yāʾ; among them are those who put kasra on the first yāʾ; and among them are those who put fatḥa on the first yāʾ and replace the second with an alif — just as they said رأيت الزيدان, replacing the yāʾ with an alif — so they say ياجل.
«[Translator's note: the printed text reads «يَا جلّ»; the intended form is evidently ياجل.]»

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying {كَمَا أخرجك رَبك من بَيْتك}: the kāf in كما is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), a naʿt (adjective) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of يجادلونك, i.e. "a disputing like…". It has been said that it is a naʿt of a maṣdar indicated by the meaning of the speech, its implied form being: "Say: the spoils are established for Allah and the Messenger, an establishing like [the way] your Lord brought you out". It has been said that it is a naʿt of حقا, i.e. "they are the believers truly, like…". It has been said that the kāf is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), the implied form being: "As your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth, so fear Allah", so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). And it has been said that the kāf has the meaning of the wāw of oath, i.e. "the spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger — by Him who brought you out".
«[Translator's note: the text has «نعت لحق»; the reference is to the word حَقًّا in verse 4.]»

mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying {إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ أَنَّهَا لكم}: أنّ is a badal (substitute) of إحدى, and it is badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion). إحدى is the second object of يعد, its implied form being: "And when Allah promised you possession of one of the two parties". An omitted muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) was assumed only because a promise does not fall upon concrete entities; it falls only upon events.
His saying {وَإِذ يَعدكُم}: إذ is in the position of the accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb, its implied form being: "And remember, O Muhammad, when He promised you".
It is related from ʿĀṣim that he read {بِأَلف من الْمَلَائِكَة} [as بآلُفٍ], making it the plural of ألف — a فَعْل on the pattern أفعُل, like فلس and أفلس. The confirmation of this reading is the saying of the Exalted بخمسة آلاف: آلُف is the plural of ألف for fewer than ten, and it refers to the five thousand mentioned in Āl ʿImrān.
«[Translator's note: the bracketed form بآلُفٍ is added for clarity from the explanation that follows; the text quotes the verse in its usual form.]»

mekki-muskil:9-9.t:
His saying {مُردفِينَ}: whoever reads it with fatḥa on the dāl makes it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm in ممدكم, or a naʿt (adjective) of ألف, its implied form being: "He reinforces you, followed up, with a thousand". The hāʾ in جعله refers back to the thousand (الألف), because it is masculine. It has been said that it refers to the following-up (الإرداف), indicated by His saying مردفين; it has been said that it refers to the reinforcement (الإمداد), indicated by His saying ممدكم; and it has been said that it refers to the acceptance of the supplication, indicated by the saying of the Exalted فاستجاب لكم. Likewise the hāʾ in به admits all of these aspects, and it may also refer to the good tidings (البشرى), because it has the meaning of rejoicing at good news (الاستبشار).
Whoever reads مردفين with kasra on the dāl makes it a ṣifa (adjective) of ألف, its meaning being: they were followed up by another number behind them, and the mafʿūl (object) is omitted, namely "a number". It has also been said that the meaning of the adjective is that they came after despair, i.e. they followed them up after they had called for help. Abū ʿUbayda reported that ردفني and أردفني both mean "he followed me". Most of the grammarians hold that أردفه means "he carried him behind him" and ردفه means "he followed him"; al-Naḥḥās also reported this from Abū ʿUbayd. On this basis it is not good for it to be an adjective of the angels, since it is not known of their description that they carried anyone of the people behind them.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {أَمَنَة}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying {فَوق الْأَعْنَاق}, i.e. the heads. فوق, according to al-Akhfash, is redundant (zāʾida), the meaning being "strike the necks". Al-Mubarrad said: فوق indicates the permissibility of striking their faces, because they are above the necks.
And His saying {كل بنان} means the fingers and other limbs.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t:
His saying {ذَلِك بِأَنَّهُم}: ذلك is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "the matter is that" or "that is the matter".
His saying {وَمن يُشَاقق الله}: من is conditional, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is فإن الله شديد العقاب. The referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, its implied form being: "then Allah is severe in punishment towards him".

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying {وَأَن للْكَافِرِينَ}: أنّ is in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ذلكم, and ذلكم is in the position of the nominative like the ذلك before it. Al-Farrāʾ said: وأن للكافرين is in the position of the accusative on the assumption of the omission of the preposition, i.e. "and because the disbelievers have…". It is also permissible to imply "and know that…". The hāʾ in فذوقوه refers back to ذلكم, and that is an allusion to the killing on the day of Badr.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying {زحفا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {متحرفا} and {متحيزا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied nominative pronoun in يولهم.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {مِنْهُ بلَاء}: the hāʾ in منه refers back to the victory over the polytheists; it has also been said: to the throwing.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {وَأَن الله}: أنّ is in the position of the accusative on the assumption "and because Allah…"; reading it with kasra (إنّ) as a new beginning (istiʾnāf) is also permissible.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t:
His saying {وتخونوا أماناتكم}: jussive (majzūm) by conjunction with لا تخونوا; or, if you wish, it is accusative (naṣb) as the answer to the prohibition with the wāw.
His saying {وَأَنْتُم تَسْمَعُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in تولوا; and similar to it is وهم معرضون.
«[Translator's note: the verse وأنتم تسمعون with تولوا is 8:20, not 8:27; the text is translated as it stands.]»

mekki-muskil:32-32.t:
His saying {هُوَ الْحق}: هو is a separating pronoun (fāṣila) announcing that the khabar (predicate) is definite or close to definite. It has been said that it was introduced to announce that كان is not in the sense of "occurred" and "happened", and that the khabar is still awaited. It has been said that it was introduced to announce that what follows it is a khabar, not a naʿt (adjective) of what precedes it. Al-Akhfash said: هو is redundant (zāʾida), just as ما was made redundant in فبما رحمة. The Kufans said: هو is an ʿimād (support pronoun).
«[Translator's note: the text reads «خبر بنعت», evidently for «خبر لا نعت» ("a predicate, not an adjective"), and is translated accordingly.]»

mekki-muskil:34-34.t:
His saying {أَلا يعذبهم الله}: أن is in the position of the accusative, its implied form being "from not punishing them" (من أن لا يعذبهم). Al-Akhfash mentioned that أن is redundant (zāʾida), yet he has made the verb accusative by it, and that is not the rule for a redundant particle.
And His saying {وهم يصدون}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied accusative pronoun in يعذبهم.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t:
His saying {وتصدية}: it is from صدّ يصِدّ when one clamours, and its origin is تصددة; one of the two dāls was replaced by a yāʾ. The meaning of تصدية is clamouring with clapping. It has been said that it is from صدّ يصُدّ when one prevents. And it has been said that it is from الصدى, the echo that answers your voice from a mountain or the air: as though the one who claps answers with his clapping someone who intends [to pray] in his prayer; on this view the yāʾ is radical.
المكاء is whistling; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الدعاء, and the hamza is a substitute for a wāw, because they say مكا يمكو when one blows.
Al-Aʿmash read وما كان صلاتهم with the accusative, and إلا مكاء وتصدية with the nominative. This is not permissible except in poetry out of necessity, because the noun of كان is the definite one and its khabar (predicate) is the indefinite one, according to the principles of speech, reasoning and meaning.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {أَنما غَنِمْتُم}: ما has the sense of الذي (relative noun), and the hāʾ is omitted from the ṣila (relative clause), its implied form being غنمتموه. The khabar (predicate) is فأن لله خمسه. The reason أن has fatḥa here is that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "then its ruling is that to Allah belongs its fifth". It has been said that [the second] أن emphasises the first, but this is not permissible, because the first would then remain without a khabar, and because the fāʾ would intervene between the emphasised word and its tawkīd (emphasis), and its being redundant is not good in a place such as this.

mekki-muskil:42-42.t:
His saying {والركب أَسْفَل مِنْكُم}: أسفل is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted adverb of place (ẓarf), its implied form being "and the caravan in a place lower than you". Al-Akhfash, al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī allowed أسفلُ in the nominative, on the assumption of something omitted at the start of the phrase, its implied form being "and the place of the caravan is lower than you".
His saying {من حييّ}: whoever pronounces the two yāʾs separately [حَيِيَ] makes the past follow the imperfect. Since assimilation (idghām) is not permitted in the imperfect — because its vowel is not fixed, shifting from nominative to accusative or to elision in the jussive — he treated the past like it, even though the vowel of its final radical is fixed; moreover the final radical of the past is also made quiescent when it is joined to a nominative pronoun, so in its changeability it has become like the final radical of the imperfect, and it was treated like it in being pronounced separately. As for whoever assimilates [حَيَّ], it is to distinguish between that whose final radical has a fixed vowel, such as the past, and that whose final radical has a shifting vowel, such as the imperfect in His saying أن يحيي الموتى — this may not be assimilated. So he assimilated the past because of the meeting of two identical letters, and assimilation is good because of the fixedness of the vowel on its final radical. Al-Farrāʾ alone allowed assimilation in the imperfect; no one else allowed it.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t:
His saying {إِذْ يريكهم}: the governing word of إذ is an implied verb, its implied form being: "And remember, O Muhammad, when He showed them to you".
«[Translator's note: the text reads «ذَا يريكهم», evidently for «إذ يريكهم».]»

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: And His saying {وَإِذ يريكموهم}: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first إذ. The wāw returned with the plural mīm when a pronoun is attached, because a pronoun restores elided letters to their original forms. Yūnus allowed dropping the wāw with the pronoun: he allowed يريكمهم with the mīm quiescent, and with it voweled with ḍamma without a wāw. Keeping it is better and more eloquent, and the Qurʾān came with it.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {بطرا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). البطر is to use the blessings of Allah as strength for acts of disobedience.

mekki-muskil:48-48.t: His saying {جَار}: جار is pluralised as أجوار for a small number, جيران for a large number, and also جيرة.

mekki-muskil:50-50.t: His saying {يضْربُونَ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the angels; and if you made it a ḥāl from الذين كفروا, that would be permissible. But if in the place of يضربون there were ضاربين, it would not be permissible until the pronoun were made overt, because when an active participle (ism fāʿil) runs as an adjective, a ḥāl, a khabar (predicate) or a conjunct of someone other than the one to whom it belongs, its agent pronoun may not be latent in it; it must be made overt. If you said رأيت رجلا معه امرأة ضاربها غدا أو الساعة ("I saw a man with a woman, beating her tomorrow or now"), and you put ضاربها in the nominative as an adjective of the woman, it would not be permissible until you said ضاربها هو, because the action is not hers. If you put it in the accusative as an adjective of the man, it is permissible and you would not need to make the pronoun overt, because the action is his. And if in the place of ضاربها there were يضربها, it would be permissible in both ways and there would be no need to make any pronoun overt.

mekki-muskil:51-51.t:
His saying {وَأَن الله لَيْسَ بظلام للعبيد}: أنّ is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), conjoined to ما in His saying بما قدمت; or, if you wish, in the position of the nominative on إلى ذلك, or by implying وذلك.
«[Translator's note: «على إلى ذلك» is as printed and appears corrupt; perhaps «عطفًا على ذلك» ("conjoined to ذلك") is intended.]»

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His saying {كدأب آل فِرْعَوْن}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "We did that to them, a doing like Our custom with the people of Pharaoh when they disbelieved". الدأب is custom. The second [occurrence] is like it, except that the first concerns the custom in punishing and the second the custom in changing; the implied form of the second is: "We changed [things] for them when they changed, a changing like Our custom with the people of Pharaoh when they denied".

mekki-muskil:58-58.t: His saying {فانبذ إِلَيْهِم على سَوَاء}: the mafʿūl (object) is omitted, its implied form being: "then throw back to them the covenant and fight them upon a notification from you to them". In the beginning of the verse there is another omission, its implied form being: "And if you fear treachery from a people between whom and you there is a covenant, then throw back to them that covenant", i.e. return it to them if you fear their breaking the covenant, and fight them upon a notification from you to them. This is among the subtle inimitability of the Qurʾān and its concision, since it has gathered many meanings of commands and reports in a brief wording.

mekki-muskil:59-59.t:
His saying {وَلَا يَحسبن الَّذين كفرُوا سبقوا}: whoever reads it with tāʾ makes it an address to the Prophet ﷺ, because addressing him has preceded at the beginning of the passage; الذين is the first object and سبقوا is in the position of the second object. Whoever reads it with yāʾ makes it [the verb] of the disbelievers, so it contains their pronoun, because they were mentioned earlier in His saying الذين كفروا فهم لا يؤمنون, and in His saying ثم ينقضون, ولا يتقون, لعلهم يذكرون, and His saying إليهم; so the first object is implied and سبقوا is in the position of the second, its implied form being: "And let not those who disbelieve think themselves to have outstripped". It has been said that أن is implied with سبقوا, and it stands in place of the two objects, as it does in His saying أحسب الناس أن يتركوا; its implied form being "and let not those who disbelieve think that they have outstripped". Sībawayh said concerning the saying of the Exalted أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد that its implied form is أن أعبد; then أن was dropped and the verb became nominative. It has been said that the agent in the reading of whoever reads with yāʾ is the Prophet, upon him be peace, so it is like the reading with tāʾ: الذين كفروا and سبقوا are the two objects of حسب. It has been said that the agent of حسب is implied in it, its implied form being "and let not those behind them think those who disbelieve to have outstripped", so الذين كفروا and سبقوا are the two objects of حسب.
Whoever reads أنهم لا يعجزون with fatḥa makes the speech connected to what precedes it, its implied form being "they have outstripped because they…", so أنّ is in the position of the accusative by the omission of the preposition; its meaning is: "And let not those who disbelieve think that they have escaped Allah, because they do not escape Allah". Whoever reads إنّ with kasra does so on the basis of a new beginning and a break [from what precedes].
«[Translator's note: the meaning-gloss «فاتوا من الله لأنهم لا يفوتون الله» is translated as printed.]»

mekki-muskil:60-60.t: His saying {وَآخَرين من دونهم}: accusative, conjoined to عدو الله.

mekki-muskil:64-64.t:
His saying {حَسبك الله وَمن اتبعك}: من is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the meaning of the kāf in حسبك الله, because in interpretation it is in the position of the accusative, since the meaning of حسبك الله is "Allah suffices you"; so من was conjoined according to the meaning. It has been said that من is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the name of Allah the Exalted; or as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) implied, i.e. "and those of the believers who follow you are likewise". It has been said that it is in the position of the nominative conjoined to حسب, because of the ugliness of conjoining it to the name of Allah, given the disapproval that has come regarding a person's saying "what Allah wills and you will"; were it with fāʾ or thumma, conjoining to the name of Allah, exalted be His mention, would be good.
The hāʾ in ترهبون به refers back to ما; it has been said: to the strength; it has been said: to the tethering; and it has been said: to the preparing. The strength is archery; it has been said: fortresses; and it has been said: stallions; and the tethered horses (رباط الخيل) are the mares.
«[Translator's note: ترهبون به and the following words are from 8:60, discussed here under 8:64 as printed.]»

mekki-muskil:68-68.t:
His saying {لَوْلَا كتاب من الله}: كتاب is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "were it not for a decree from Allah that overtook you". It is what was set down beforehand in the Preserved Tablet of making spoils lawful for this community. It has been said that it is what preceded, that Allah does not punish except after a warning. It has been said that it is what preceded, that Allah forgives minor sins for whoever avoids the major ones. And it has been said that it is what preceded, that Allah forgives the people of Badr their sins, past and future.
His saying {لمسكم}: the apodosis (jawāb) of لولا.

mekki-muskil:69-69.t: His saying {حَلَالا طيبا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in كلوا, or from ما.

mekki-muskil:71-71.t: His saying {خِيَانَتك}: خيانة is pluralised as خيائن. The original of the first yāʾ is wāw, because it is from خان يخون; but they distinguished by the yāʾ between it and the plural of خائنة, which is خوائن.

mekki-muskil:72-72.t: His saying {من ولايتهم}: whoever reads the wāw with fatḥa makes it the maṣdar (verbal noun) of ولي; one says "he is a protector (ولي) and patron (مولى), evident in الوَلاية" with fatḥa. Whoever reads the wāw with kasra makes it the maṣdar of الوالي; one says "he is a governor (وال), evident in الوِلاية". It has also been said that they are two dialectal forms of the maṣdar of الولي.

mekki-muskil:73-73.t: His saying {إِلَّا تفعلوه}: the hāʾ refers back to mutual support; it has also been said that it refers back to mutual inheritance, i.e. "if you do not practise inheritance among relatives as Allah has prescribed for you, and abandon inheritance by emigration, there will be fitna in the land and corruption"; "if you do not practise mutual support in religion, there will be fitna in the land and great corruption through disbelief".
